chunks.sanskrit: saṃkrāmo 'tra na bhāvanā na ca kathāyuktir na carcā na ca dhyānaṃ vā na ca dhāraṇā na ca japābhyāsaprayāso na ca | tat kiṃ nāma suniścitaṃ vada paraṃ satyaṃ ca tac chrūyatām: na tyāgī na parigrahī — bhaja sukhaṃ sarvam yathāvasthitaḥ
chunks.l1:
## anu-p01 (1)
transition / here / not / contemplation / nor / connection-of-speech / nor / discussion / nor / visualization / or / nor / steadying / nor / japa-practice-effort / That / what / name / well-decided / speak / supreme / truth / and / that / hear / not / renouncer / not / possessor / enjoy / happiness / all / as-staying
chunks.l2: Transition here is no method at all — not contemplation, not speech-connection, not discussion, not visualization, not steadying, not japa-practice-effort. So what is well-decided? Speak the supreme truth, and hear it: not renouncer, not possessor — enjoy happiness, wholly, as staying.
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p01 — argument map

Six techniques denied: contemplation, speech-connection, discussion, visualization, steadying, japa-practice-effort. The question replaces the hunt: what stands well-decided? Speak it, hear it. The answer is two refusals and one command: not renouncer, not possessor — enjoy happiness, wholly, as staying. Staying (yathāvasthita) is the method that is no method — anupāya named by performance, not by label.

### Open
- Whether 'suniścita' (well-decided) is an adjective of truth or a separate noun is unresolved.
- Whether 'japābhyāsaprayāso na ca' is one token or several is unresolved (kept as printed).

chunks.sanskrit: saṃsāro 'sti na tattvatas tanubhṛtāṃ bandhasya vārtaiva kā bandho yasya na jātu tasya vitathā muktasya muktikriyā | mithyāmohakṛd eṣa rajjubhujagacchāyāpiśācabhramo mā kiṃcit tyaja mā gṛhāṇa vihara [1] svastho yathāvasthitaḥ || AgAna_2

pūjapūjakapūjyabhedasaraṇiḥ keyaṃ kathānuttare saṃkrāmaḥ kila kasya kena vidadhe ko vā praveśakramaḥ | māyeyam na cidadvayāt paratayā bhinnāpy aho vartate sarvaṃ svānubhavasvabhāvavimalaṃ cintāṃ vṛthā mā kṛthāḥ || AgAna_3

ānando 'tra na vittamadhyamadavan naivāṅganāsaṅgavat dīpārkendukṛtaprabhāprakaravan naiva prakāśodayaḥ | harṣaḥ saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr bhārāvatāropamaḥ sarvādvaitapadasya vismṛtanidheḥ prāptiḥ prakāśodayaḥ || AgAna_4

rāgadveṣasukhāsukhodayalayāhaṅkāradainyādayo ye bhāvāḥ pravibhānti viśvavapuṣo bhinnasvabhāvā na te | vyaktiṃ paśyasi yasya yasya sahasā tattattadekātmatāsaṃvidrūpam avekṣya kiṃ na ramase tadbhāvanānirbharaḥ || AgAna_5
chunks.l1:
## anu-p05 (5)
Passion / aversion / pleasure / displeasure / rise / dissolution / I-ness / misery / and-the-rest / those / things / shining-forth / universe-bodied / different-natured / not / Manifestation / you-see / of-whom / suddenly / that-that / one-self-natured / consciousness-form / having-regarded / why / do-you-delight / with-that / contemplation-full
chunks.l2: Passion, aversion, pleasure, displeasure, rise and fall, I-ness, misery and the rest — things shining forth, universe-bodied, are not different-natured. Whosever manifestation you suddenly see — having regarded it as one-self-natured consciousness-form — why do you not delight, full of contemplation?
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p05 — argument map

Passion, aversion, pleasure, displeasure, rise, dissolution, I-ness, misery and the rest — things shining-forth, universe-bodied — are not different-natured. Whosever manifestation you suddenly see — having regarded (avekṣya) that-that (tattattad) one-self-natured (ekātmatā) consciousness-form (saṃvidrūpam) — Why (kiṃ na) do you delight (ramase), full (nirbharaḥ) of that contemplation (tadbhāvanā)? Regard is the whole practice: see variety as one-self-natured consciousness-form — delight is the only consistent response.

### Open
- Whether 'ekātmatāsaṃvidrūpa' is one compound or several is unresolved.
- Whether 'ramase' is indicative or imperative is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: pūrvābhāvabhavakriyā hi sahasā bhāvāḥ sadā 'smin bhave madhyākāravikārasaṃkaravatāṃ teṣāṃ kutaḥ satyatā | niḥsatye capale prapañcanicaye svapnabhrame peśale śaṅkātaṅkakalaṅkayuktikalanātītaḥ prabuddho bhava || AgAna_6
chunks.l1:
## anu-p06 (6)
Former / non-being / being / action / indeed / suddenly / things / always / in-this / existence / middle-formed / transformation / confusion / of-them / whence / truth / In-non-truth / unsteady / manifold / dream-delusion / clever / from-doubt- fear-stain-reasoning-transcended / awakened / become
chunks.l2: Former non-being, being, action — things always, suddenly, in this existence: middle-formed, transformation-confused — whence their truth? In the non-true, unsteady, manifold, clever dream-delusion — transcending doubt, fear, stain, and reasoning's contriving: awakened, become.
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p06 — argument map

Former non-being (pūrvābhāva), being (bhava), action (kriyā) — indeed (hi) suddenly (sahasā) things (bhāvāḥ) always (sadā) in this existence (asmin bhave) — of middle-formed (madhyākāra) transformation (vikāra), confusion (saṃkaravatāṃ) of them (teṣām): whence (kutaḥ) truth (satyatā)? In non-truth (niḥsatye), unsteady (capale), manifold (prapañcanicaye), dream-delusion (svapnabhrame), clever (peśale) — From doubt-fear-stain-reasoning-contriving transcended (śaṅkātaṅkakalaṅkayuktikalanātītaḥ): awakened (prabuddhaḥ), become (bhava). Four obstacles — doubt, fear, stain, reasoning — with reasoning listed last among the fetters.

### Open
- Whether 'madhyākāra' means middle-formed or of middle-form is unresolved.
- Whether 'peśala' means clever or cunning is unresolved.
- Whether 'bhava' (become) is imperative or indicative is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: bhāvānāṃ na samudbhavo 'sti sahajas tvadbhāvitā bhānty amī niḥsatyā api satyatām anubhavabhrāntyā bhajanti kṣaṇam | tvatsaṅkalpaja eṣa viśvamahimā nāsty asya janmānyataḥ tasmāt tvaṃ vibhavena bhāsi bhuvaneṣv ekopy anekātmakaḥ || AgAna_7
chunks.l1:
## anu-p07 (7)
Of-things / no / arising / natural / by-your-contemplation / they-shine / non-true / truth / by-experience-delusion / partake / for-a-moment / This / universe-glory / from-your-will-born / not / its / birth / from-elsewhere / Hence / you / by-splendor / shine / in-worlds / one / many-selfed
chunks.l2: Of things there is no arising; naturally, by your contemplation they shine; even the non-true partakes of truth for a moment, through experience's delusion. This universe-glory is will-born from you, birth from elsewhere it has none; hence by splendor you shine in worlds — one, yet many-selfed.
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p07 — argument map

Of things (bhāvānām) no arising (na samudbhavaḥ) is — natural (sahajaḥ), by your contemplation (tvadbhāvitā) they shine (bhānti). Non-true (niḥsatyāḥ) too (api), truth (satyatām) they partake (bhajanti) by experience-delusion (anubhavabhrāntyā) for a moment (kṣaṇam). This universe-glory (eṣa viśvamahimā) will-born from you (tvatsaṅkalpajaḥ); its birth (janma) from elsewhere (anyataḥ) is not (nāsti). Hence (tasmāt) you shine (bhāsi) by splendor (vibhavena) in worlds (bhuvaneṣu) — one (ekaḥ), though (api), many-selfed (anekātmakaḥ).

### Open
- Whether 'sahaja' means 'natural' or 'innate' is unresolved.
- Whether 'anubhavabhrānti' means experience's delusion or delusion of experience is unresolved.
- Whether 'ekopy anekātmakaḥ' means 'one, though many-selfed' or 'one, yet (becoming) many-selfed' is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: yat satyaṃ yad asatyam alpabahulaṃ nityaṃ na nityaṃ ca yat yan māyāmalinaṃ yad ātmavimalaṃ ciddarpaṇe rājate | tat sarvaṃ svavimarśasaṃvidudayād rūpaprakāśātmakaṃ jñātvā svānubhavādhirūḍhamahimā viśveśvaratvaṃ bhaja || AgAna_8
chunks.l1:
## anu-p08 (8)
What / true / what / untrue / little-much / eternal / not / eternal / what / Māyā-stained / what / self-pure / in- consciousness-mirror / shines / That / all / from-own-grasping-consciousness-rise / form-light-natured / having-known / own-experience-risen / glory / Lordhood / worship
chunks.l2: What true, what untrue, little-much, eternal, not eternal, what Māyā-stained, what self-pure — in the consciousness-mirror shines. That all, from own-grasping-consciousness-rise, form-light-natured, having known — own-experience-risen glory: Lordhood — worship.
chunks.argmap:
## anu-p08 — argument map

What true, what untrue, little-much, eternal, not eternal, what Māyā-stained, what self-pure — shines (rājate) in the consciousness-mirror (ciddarpaṇe). All opposites, one mirror; the mirror doesn't sort them. That all (tat sarvaṃ), from own-grasping-consciousness-rise (svavimarśasaṃvidudayāt), form-light-natured (rūpaprakāśātmakam), having known (jñātvā) — — own-experience-risen (svānubhavādhirūḍha) glory (mahimā): Lordhood (viśveśvaratvam) — worship (bhaja).

### Open
- Whether 'svavimarśasaṃvidudaya' is one compound or several is unresolved.
- Whether 'rūpaprakāśātmaka' modifies 'tat sarvam' or 'mahimā' is unresolved.
- Whether 'bhaja' is imperative or indicative is unresolved.
